classification.difficultyReason: Every part is a reverse chain rule integral of the form f'(x)e^{f(x)} with a constant multiple to adjust. No 'hence' or differentiation hint is given, so the student must pick out the inner function, differentiate it mentally and compensate with the right constant. Part (c) needs a factor of 1/4. Part (e) needs a sign change after rewriting 1/x² as x^{-2}. Part (f) is the hardest. The student must rewrite -x√x as -x^{3/2}, find the derivative -3/2·√x and use the factor 2/3. This is a routine linked procedure with no hidden insight. It is slightly above p61-q18, where the hint supplies the derivative. It is below p62-q19, which mixes trig substitutions with a general exponent n and definite limits.
